summary: fits stress = consistency * rate ^ flow_index to a flow curve and returns both with the residual

inputs.name: shear_rate
inputs.meaning: the shear rates of the flow curve, a list

inputs.name: shear_stress
inputs.meaning: the shear stress at each rate, a list of the same length

outputs.name: fitted
outputs.meaning: true when a fit was made

outputs.name: flow_index
outputs.meaning: the exponent of the power law

outputs.name: consistency
outputs.meaning: the stress at a shear rate of one reciprocal second; its unit carries the flow index

outputs.name: residual_rms_log
outputs.meaning: root mean square of the residuals of ln(stress)

outputs.name: basis
outputs.meaning: how the numbers were computed, naming this skill and its version

validity: a power-law fluid over the range of the points; a yield stress or a Newtonian plateau is another model and another skill

source.citation: C. W. Macosko, Rheology: Principles, Measurements, and Applications, 1994
source.locus: the power-law model of the viscosity of a generalised Newtonian fluid: stress = m * rate ^ n

note: On fixture data handed in as inputs (meta_agent/tests/fixtures/rheometer/inputs/flow_curve.json). The locus has not been checked against the book by a seat.
